topics.topic: Required test coverage for revalidating the cross-bound runtime-settings constraint on every load
questions: What Required test must show that `binary_storage` actually calls `load_runtime_settings` at each read and rechecks the read-bound/response-ceiling constraint after a successful start, rather than caching the start-up result?

Must the CFG-001 test demonstrate that the cross-bound constraint is rechecked on every invocation of `load_runtime_settings`, including invocations by the bootstrap command, `registry_gateway`, and `binary_storage`, or is demonstrating refusal during service start sufficient?

quotes: The start-up check that the read bound is no larger than the response ceiling is a constraint of that table (`BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` less than or equal to `MAX_BINARY_RESPONSE_BYTES`), checked by `runtime_settings` at each `load_runtime_settings`, so a violating deployment does not start; `binary_storage` applies only the read bound, at each read.

The emitted
  `binary_storage` takes both from the settings `load_runtime_settings`
  returns, which it calls at each read, as its backend IR
  (`binary_storage_backend` schema version 2, `settings`) names them, and
  reads no environment itself (owner 2026-11-09, SPEC_STANDARD 6.11;
  Factory code-factory #201).

CFG-001: one check per bound, each with the bound at its value: a Registry
  request that outlasts the timeout fails as the `timeout` member of
  `RegistryFailureKind`; a staff session and a viewer session are refused
  from the instant their issue time plus their lifetime is reached; the
  viewer-entry attempt after the limit within the window is refused and
  creates no session; a request body over its bound and a binary over its
  read bound are refused before the handler or the response; and the start
  is refused when the read bound exceeds the response bound, which is how
  `max_binary_response_bytes` is applied: no module compares a response with
  it, and every binary sent is within the read bound and so within it.
judgement.divergence: One verifier demonstrates only refusal during service startup, while another changes the settings after startup and demonstrates refusal on a later binary read; the implementing and verification agents notice that only the latter proves the required per-call reload and cross-bound revalidation.
judgement.why: CFG-001 requires only a startup-refusal example even though the rule requires validation on every loader call and a fresh loader call at every binary read, so it does not say that the per-call invariant must be shown.

witness.initial: The service has started with the read bound no greater than the response ceiling, and an authorized deliverable binary exists.
events: A verification agent performs a successful authorized binary read.
The verification agent changes the deployment settings so `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` exceeds `MAX_BINARY_RESPONSE_BYTES`.
The verification agent performs a second authorized binary read.
outcomes: A suite that proves the stated per-call rule refuses the second read because `load_runtime_settings` revalidates the changed bounds.
A suite implementing only the listed startup-refusal check need not exercise the second read and can accept an implementation that caches the startup settings.
witness.observer: The implementing agent and verification agent.
basis:
The emitted
  `binary_storage` takes both from the settings `load_runtime_settings`
  returns, which it calls at each read, as its backend IR
  (`binary_storage_backend` schema version 2, `settings`) names them, and
  reads no environment itself (owner 2026-11-09, SPEC_STANDARD 6.11;
  Factory code-factory #201).

A deployment value is a row of `config.runtime_environment_variables` read only by `load_runtime_settings`, into a field of `RuntimeSettings` (`database_url`, `environment`, `public_origin`, `trusted_hosts`, `allowed_origins`, `max_request_body_bytes`, `max_binary_response_bytes`, `production_logging`, the two viewer-entry limits and, since 2026-11-09, `registry_base_url`, `binary_storage_root` and `binary_max_read_bytes`); the emitted `binary_storage` reads the last two from the settings `load_runtime_settings` returns, like every other reader.

topics.topic: Bootstrap command outcome and exit-code mapping for runtime-settings constraint failure
questions: When the new read-bound/response-ceiling constraint fails while the first-administrator bootstrap command calls `load_runtime_settings`, how is that refusal represented relative to the closed `BootstrapCommandOutcome` and `BOOTSTRAP_EXIT_CODES` catalogs?

quotes:
Each refusal is its exit code. A configuration or storage failure is none of
the four outcomes: the operation raises it and returns no exit code, and the
failure status the host process then ends with is outside the closed
contract of A29.
judgement.why: The later public-operation contract says a runtime-configuration failure is outside the four bootstrap outcomes, is raised rather than mapped through `BOOTSTRAP_EXIT_CODES`, and returns no contractual exit code.

topics.topic: Precedence between per-read runtime-settings validation and binary storage validation failures
questions: When a per-read settings load finds an invalid bound relation and the referenced binary would also fail storage resolution, size, or signature validation, which check wins and which failure is returned?

quotes:
The emitted `binary_storage`
  takes the storage root and the read limit the same way, from the
  `binary_storage_root` and `binary_max_read_bytes` fields of the settings
  `load_runtime_settings` returns, which it calls at each binary read, and
  refuses that read as `BinaryStorageError` when the settings cannot be
  loaded (owner 2026-11-09; `binary_storage_backend` schema version 2).
judgement.why: The later module text requires the settings load on each read and refuses the read as `BinaryStorageError` when that load fails; because the storage root needed for resolution comes from that load, storage resolution does not precede the failed settings validation.

topics.topic: Response for an authorized document record whose stored content is missing
questions: When an authorized ExpenseDocument record exists but its stored content is missing, must the response be an explicit unavailable/not-found failure as A14 says, or the concealed response used for unknown, cross-project, and hidden document reads as R0-12 says?

quotes:
Document: missing record, other project, hidden, missing object, oversize
  or unlisted media type: one concealed not-found answer (404). Photo:
  missing record, other project or hidden: one validation refusal (422);
  stored content that cannot be delivered (missing object, oversize,
  unlisted type): storage-unavailable failure (500), as State 0 R0-12
  says. Nothing is written.
judgement.why: The later flow explicitly decides that a missing object for an expense document receives the same concealed 404 not-found answer as a missing, cross-project, or hidden record.

topics.topic: Service behavior and caller-visible failure when runtime settings become invalid during a binary read
questions: If the deployment passed start-up but `load_runtime_settings` finds the bound relation invalid during a later binary read, does only that read fail, does the service terminate, or is the last valid configuration retained; and which typed failure reaches the caller?

judgement.why: P5 already judges the same post-start binary-read settings-load failure and its caller-visible translation, and the relevant passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Binary-read behavior when runtime settings become missing, empty, or malformed after startup
quotes:
The emitted `binary_storage`
  takes the storage root and the read limit the same way, from the
  `binary_storage_root` and `binary_max_read_bytes` fields of the settings
  `load_runtime_settings` returns, which it calls at each binary read, and
  refuses that read as `BinaryStorageError` when the settings cannot be
  loaded (owner 2026-11-09; `binary_storage_backend` schema version 2).

read_expense_document: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST translate a BinaryStorageError raised by read_binary into BinaryAccessRejected; it owns no transaction guard, because the only transaction is the one _authorize_document_reference opens and closes.

`PhotoValidationError` for a missing, another project's or an invisible
photo; `BinaryStorageError` for an unreadable object. Unlike documents, the
accepted service does not fold these into one answer.

_registry_url: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST join only the supplied relative path to the Registry deployment URL, which is the registry_base_url field of the RuntimeSettings that the imported load_runtime_settings returns when this function calls it, and MUST preserve that URL's own path prefix so a Registry deployed under a prefix keeps it on every request; it MUST NOT read the process environment itself. A missing or empty URL never reaches this function, because load_runtime_settings refuses the service start for it, and this function MUST NOT catch, translate or repair a refusal of load_runtime_settings. Each of the following MUST raise RegistryBoundaryError carrying the TRANSPORT_ERROR member of = models.RegistryFailureKind, never a raw ValueError or other untyped error, and never a repaired URL: the URL is not a usable http or https base URL; it carries userinfo credentials, which are rejected rather than stripped, retained, or forwarded; the supplied path is absolute or protocol-relative, which MUST NOT be allowed to replace the host or scheme.

Any other failure is 500. No failure becomes a success, an empty list or a
  zero, except in the two reads whose Errors say so:
  `derived_views.build_project_overview` turns a part's failure into that
  part's availability, and `derived_views.list_viewer_projects` leaves out a
  project whose Registry context fails.
precedent.why: Later module, note, and API texts require every failed binary-settings reload to become BinaryStorageError, concealed as BinaryAccessRejected for documents and exposed for photos, while a Registry settings-load refusal is neither cached nor translated and therefore follows the generic 500 mapping.
